Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: full-width illustrated worldbook scene, landscape 3:2, approximately 1536 x 1024.
Primary request: A striking, hopeful near-future cooperative community building civilian rockets to explore outer space together. Show the CULTURE of exploration and the grand physical ambition, on Earth.
Scene and composition: Looking from a welcoming mission commons and observatory terrace into an immense robot-assisted integration hangar through broad glazing. In the foreground, diverse adult neighbors, older people, and a teenager gather around a tactile model and discuss a star chart without readable lettering; some look through an elegant telescope. Beyond the glass, a spectacular large reusable civilian rocket lies horizontally undergoing final assembly, with a few clearly robotic manipulators and service platforms. Beyond the hangar through the open distant view, a coastal launch tower with a second upright rocket is separated from the community by a long stretch of empty coastal terrain. Gardens, walking paths, homes, and the mission commons belong to the human settlement; the distant launch area is legibly separate.
Style/medium: Rich editorial architectural concept art, realistic materials, beautiful spatial clarity and scale, intricate but legible, warm daylight with blue coastal distance, no generic billionaire showroom atmosphere.
Meaning: People live here through a shared ambition to understand the cosmos. Sophisticated autonomous production supports voluntary exploration; civilian community, thoughtful wonder.
Constraints: New unique composition. No readable text, logos, flags, branding, weapons, soldiers, corporate headquarters, aliens or alien planet. Rocket depiction is visual concept art, no engineering diagram. No comic panels. Landscape 3:2.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: full-width illustrated worldbook scene, landscape 3:2, approximately 1536 x 1024.
Primary request: Show a lived MMORPG-like civic world: a real inhabited, walkable fantasy-inspired near-future town at blue hour, where people collectively author and inhabit a persistent shared story.
Scene and composition: At street level, an inviting winding town square with arcades, little homes, public kitchens, workshops, planted balconies, and fantastical towers that are plausible built architecture. In the foreground and middle ground, a diverse group of ordinary adults in imaginative handmade guild clothing collaborate on a luminous circular communal quest-map installation. Their body language is friendly anticipation of a shared expedition or festival, not a battle. A gorgeous translucent augmented-reality celestial creature made of starlight flows above the square and guides an illuminated trail through the arcades. Some participants wear subtle lightweight AR glasses; some inhabitants read, eat dinner, carry groceries, or watch from balconies. A small autonomous service cart discreetly tends everyday infrastructure. Show the narrative world filling the real place; it's a city people live in, not a tabletop gaming room or dance studio.
Style/medium: Rich detailed editorial architectural concept art with believable people and building materials, wondrous luminous indigo and amber evening, coherent spatial depth, generous imaginative scale. Persistent shared narrative and everyday belonging.
Constraints: New unique composition. No violence, weapons, enemy, leaderboard, score, game HUD or UI overlays, readable text, logos, licensed franchise characters. Avoid dystopia, neon cyberpunk advertising, generic suburban lifestyle. Landscape 3:2.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: full-width two-panel experiential storyboard for illustrated worldbook, landscape 3:2, approximately 1536 x 1024.
Primary request: Render how an ordinary elevator becomes a shared experiential teleport through immersive AR and designed environments. TWO EQUAL VERTICAL PANELS in one wide image, separated by a single thin clean divider, no lettering. Same camera position looking from the back of the same elevator cabin out its open doors in both panels. The transformation of experienced reality must be spectacular and unmistakable.
LEFT PANEL: An elegant, ordinary near-future elevator cabin with brushed metal doorway, a distinctive teal upholstered bench along the left wall, curved wooden handrail on the right, level threshold, soft ceiling strip light. Three ordinary adult friends are inside, seen from behind at the doorway: a woman with short dark hair wearing a terracotta jacket, an older man wearing a cream shirt, a woman with dark skin wearing a blue coat. One wears subtle AR glasses. Open doors reveal their grounded garden-city departure: a planted courtyard, real paths, warm stone arcades and daylight.
RIGHT PANEL: Exactly the same cabin framing, same teal bench, same curved handrail, same ceiling light, same doorframe, same three adults with identical clothing and positions, now showing delight. The open doors fill the entire external view with an extraordinary luminous cloud-island harbor: floating-looking terraces, radiant sails, cascading gardens above a sea of pearlescent clouds. An inviting wide bridge begins level with the elevator threshold and leads into this immersive world. This is their constructed shared perceptual destination through AR/theatrical spatial design, not an engineering depiction of literal physical teleportation. Show one subtle pearlescent shimmer at the door edge to suggest an experiential layer. The world should fill their experience with scale and depth, not look like a small painting or screen pasted onto a wall.
Style/medium: Beautiful realistic architectural concept art, rich coherent lighting. Human wonder. Each half composition is carefully parallel so viewers instantly understand departure/arrival in the same elevator.
Constraints: Exactly two panels, equal widths, single thin divider. No text, arrows, captions, numbers, UI HUD, logos, violence, or cartoon style. No extra panels. Do not replace the ordinary cabin with a science-fiction teleportation machine. Landscape 3:2.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: inspiring full-width cover illustration for a worldbook, landscape 3:2, approximately 1536 x 1024, no text.
Primary request: A civilization learning to consciously shape the worlds it inhabits. Render the meta-level of hopeful worldbuilding: diverse residents jointly imagining, discussing, and physically modelling the future of their shared world.
Scene and composition: An expansive open civic design pavilion in a living garden city. Main foreground focus: an elegant very large tactile modular landscape model, surrounded by a small group of varied adults and older people, with one observing child. They are thinking together, moving a modular building piece, sketching, pointing, listening; an equal community conversation, not a presenter lecturing passive workers. The beautifully crafted model clearly contains different possible ways of living: a lush garden district, an open university, a fantastical narrative quarter with arcades and bridges, and a peaceful exploration complex with observatory and slender civilian rocket. A subtle translucent AI-assisted spatial projection floats over a small part of the model; no symbols or text.
Behind the group, the actual city stretches into clear daytime distance: diverse planted public architecture, a striking experience tower housing shared imaginative worlds, and far beyond the lived settlement a separated coastal spaceport with a small rocket visible on its distant tower. Wide sky and calm spatial legibility balance human scale and civilization-scale ambition. Ground the scene in Earth materials and a collective sense of generosity, curiosity, and agency.
Style/medium: Sophisticated rich editorial architectural concept art, cinematic daylight, natural human expressions, warm stone and wood, assembled metal structures, lush green planting, lucid beautiful composition. The model is recognizably tactile and hypothetical, never presented as factual geography.
Constraints: Brand-new unique cover composition. No readable text, maps with labels, logos, flags, weapons, corporate boardroom, hologram dashboards, tokens or financial imagery. No duplicate use of previous garden-scene composition. No futuristic bodysuits. Landscape 3:2.
